title: Jeff Regan, Investigator
paragraphs: A hard-boiled private-eye series about Jeff Regan, an investigator working for a detective agency and handling murder, blackmail, missing persons, and other cases in postwar Los Angeles.

Regional CBS West Coast private-eye drama created by E. Jack Neuman. Jeff Regan works for Anthony J. Lyon at the International Detective Bureau. The frozen GRH container includes four OTRR reference tracks, two rehearsals, and 53 broadcast objects covering 52 unique broadcast dates because one date survives in both network and AFRS form.

GRH documents the program through Jack Webb first run (July 10, 1948 to December 18, 1948) on [[org|org.5d1a575385a05456|CBS Pacific Network]] and Frank Graham / Paul Dubov revival (October 5, 1949 to September 3, 1950) on [[org|org.5d1a575385a05456|CBS Pacific Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Sterling Tracy (producer on 28 recordings, director on 18 recordings, and transcriber on 2 recordings), Bob Stevenson (announcer on 29 recordings), Richard Aurandt (organist on 18 recordings, music on 6 recordings, composer on 2 recordings, and performer on 2 recordings), Frank Nelson (performer on 21 recordings), [[person|jack-webb|Jack Webb]] (performer on 20 recordings), E. Jack Neuman (writer on 18 recordings), and Frank Graham (performer on 16 recordings).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.5d1a575385a05456|CBS Pacific Network]] (broadcast on network) and [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include murder and homicide, fraud, theft and confidence schemes, missing persons and disappearance, Los Angeles and Southern California, police, detectives and investigation, and blackmail, extortion and threats.
GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Postwar private-eye boom, Regional network production, 1949 revival softens the lead, and Military rebroadcast preservation.
